title: Food License (FSSAI)
blocks: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is like a rule-keeper for making sure that the food we eat in India is safe and clean. All the people or businesses involved in making, selling, or delivering food must get registered with FSSAI. This registration process makes sure that these businesses follow the laws about food safety. This page gives you a quick look at how to get registered with FSSAI, why it’s important, what you need before applying, and what you’ll get after registration. We also have answers to common questions about this process.
FSSAI registration guarantees that food business operators (FBOs) follow the food safety laws and regulations in India.
FBOs with registration can expand their market reach, gaining access to broader opportunities such as government tenders and exports.
FSSAI registration boosts consumers’ trust in the safety and quality of food products and services provided by food business operators (FBOs).
Adhering to FSSAI guidelines and standards results in enhanced operational efficiency and lowers the risk of foodborne illnesses.

FSSAI registration is a basic requirement for small-scale food businesses with an annual turnover below INR 12 lakhs. FSSAI license is mandatory for medium and large-scale food businesses and is categorized into State and Central licenses based on the scale and nature of the business. .
The validity period of an FSSAI registration/license ranges from 1 to 5 years, depending on the duration chosen by the applicant. The registration/license must be renewed before the expiry date. .

The FSSAI registration process typically takes around 7-10 working days for Basic registration and 30-60 days for State or Central licenses, depending on the complexity of the food business and the FSSAI’s processing time. .

Operating a food business without a valid FSSAI registration/license may result in penalties, fines, and legal consequences. Penalties may vary depending on the specific offense and the severity of the violation. .
